### Problem: zigzag level order {#sec-tv-p3-zigzag}

::: {.p-statement}
Return the level order, left to right on even levels (the root is level $0$) and right to left on odd levels.

Constraints: up to $2000$ nodes.

Source: [LC 103 · Binary Tree Zigzag Level Order Traversal](https://leetcode.com/problems/binary-tree-zigzag-level-order-traversal/){.solved difficulty="Medium"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
Collect every level left to right. Reverse the odd ones. Alternating the push order of a **queue** does not reverse the next level, because a queue does not reverse. A stack does.
:::

::: {.p-approach}
1. **Reverse.** Ordinary level order. Reverse the row when its index is odd.
2. **Place.** Write the $i$-th node of an odd level at index $s - 1 - i$, so the row is never reversed afterwards.
3. **Two stacks.** Pop one stack for this level and push its children onto the other. Left then right while the level is even; right then left while it is odd. The next pop is already the zigzag order, because a stack reverses.

**Invariant.** Children are pushed left to right, so the $i$-th pop of a round is the $i$-th node from the left. Even levels keep that index. Odd levels want it from the right.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset .solution-forms}

#### Reverse

::: {.form-next}
Level $0$ is stored as collected. Only odd levels are reversed.
:::

```{python}

#| renderings: [light, dark]

    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("zig", "rev")
    assert str(final) == "[[3], [20, 9], [15, 7]]"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

##### Python

```{python}
def zigzag_reverse(root):
    if root is None:
        return []
    q, out = deque([root]), []
    while q:
        level = []
        for _ in range(len(q)):
            u = q.popleft()
            level.append(u.val)
            if u.left:
                q.append(u.left)
            if u.right:
                q.append(u.right)
        if len(out) % 2 == 1:
            level.reverse()
        out.append(level)
    return out
```

##### C++

```cpp
vector<vector<int>> zigzagLevelOrder(TreeNode* root) {
    vector<vector<int>> out;
    if (!root) return out;
    queue<TreeNode*> q;
    q.push(root);
    while (!q.empty()) {
        int s = (int)q.size();
        vector<int> level;
        for (int i = 0; i < s; ++i) {
            auto u = q.front();
            q.pop();
            level.push_back(u->val);
            if (u->left) q.push(u->left);
            if (u->right) q.push(u->right);
        }
        if (out.size() % 2 == 1) reverse(level.begin(), level.end());
        out.push_back(level);
    }
    return out;
}
```

:::

#### Place

::: {.form-next}
Same pops. The odd row is filled from the right as the nodes arrive, so there is no second pass over the row.
:::

```{python}

#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("zig", "place")
    assert str(final) == "[[3], [20, 9], [15, 7]]"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

##### Python

```{python}
def zigzag_place(root):
    if root is None:
        return []
    q, out, d = deque([root]), [], 0
    while q:
        s = len(q)
        level = [0] * s
        for i in range(s):
            u = q.popleft()
            level[i if d % 2 == 0 else s - 1 - i] = u.val
            if u.left:
                q.append(u.left)
            if u.right:
                q.append(u.right)
        out.append(level)
        d += 1
    return out


z = from_level([3, 9, 20, None, None, 15, 7])
assert zigzag_reverse(z) == zigzag_place(z) == [[3], [20, 9], [15, 7]]
assert zigzag_reverse(None) == []
assert zigzag_reverse(Node(1)) == [[1]]
assert zigzag_reverse(from_level([1, 2, 3, None, 4, 5])) == [[1], [3, 2], [4, 5]]
```

```cpp
// Same BFS. On an odd level write level[s - 1 - i] instead of reversing afterwards.
```

#### Two stacks

::: {.form-next}
Pop the current stack. Push children onto the other stack, left then right on an even level and right then left on an odd level. The next pop is the zigzag row.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("zig", "stacks")
    assert str(final) == "[[3], [20, 9], [15, 7]]"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

##### Python

```{python}
def zigzag_stacks(root):
    if root is None:
        return []
    cur, nxt = [root], []
    out, left_to_right = [], True
    while cur:
        row = []
        while cur:
            u = cur.pop()
            row.append(u.val)
            kids = (u.left, u.right) if left_to_right else (u.right, u.left)
            for c in kids:
                if c is not None:
                    nxt.append(c)
        out.append(row)
        cur, nxt = nxt, cur
        left_to_right = not left_to_right
    return out


z = from_level([3, 9, 20, None, None, 15, 7])
assert zigzag_stacks(z) == [[3], [20, 9], [15, 7]]
assert zigzag_stacks(from_level([1, 2, 3, None, 4, 5])) == [[1], [3, 2], [4, 5]]
assert zigzag_stacks(from_level([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7])) == [[1], [3, 2], [4, 5, 6, 7]]
```

##### C++

```cpp
// Two stacks. Even level: push left, then right. Odd level: push right, then left.
```

:::

:::

::: {.p-complexity}
$O(n)$ time, $O(w)$ extra memory besides the output.
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- The empty tree is `[]`. One node is `[[1]]`.
- `[3,9,20,null,null,15,7]` is `[[3],[20,9],[15,7]]`. Reversing even levels fails this tree.
- A left spine has one node per level, so the reversal is invisible.
- `[1,2,3,null,4,5]` is `[[1],[3,2],[4,5]]`. The gap does not change the left-to-right collection order.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistakes"}
- Alternating the push order of a queue does not reverse the next level. On `[1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9]` that push order prints `[[1],[2,3],[5,4,7,6],[8,9]]`.
- Level $0$ is left to right. An off-by-one in the parity reverses the root's row and every even row after it.
:::

**Variants.** Reversing the values on the odd levels of a perfect tree writes these rows back into the nodes. The right side view keeps the node popped at index $s - 1$ of each round (@sec-tv-level). Bottom-up zigzag reverses the list of rows after they exist; the parity is still counted from the root.
